World War II is my favorite piece of history and I've always enjoyed Hollywood's take of it. From Saving Private Ryan to Inglorious Bastards, I've always been a sucker for a good WWII flick. Hacksaw Ridge ranks among the best films depicting the great World War and while not Gibson's best work, it still proves he remains to be in a caliber of his own.

Pros:

-beautifully shot

-raw action sequences

-great acting all around

Cons:

-a couple of instances of poor CGI... The very first death in the movie especially.

-Andrew Garfield. His acting was great, but I just couldnt help but think to myself every time he was on the screen that he could've easily been a lesbian. I don't know if its the hair or what, but it was almost distracting.

I could just be a weirdo for that last one, but don't let a lesbian keep you from watching one of the best movies of the year.
Hacksaw Ridge was pretty damn good.

Idk. Kinda comes off as a bad moral if you ask me. Glorifying the twink lesbian who's brave enough to die for his country but not brave enough to kill for it? Not exactly the kind of message I'd want to be giving my kids. It's not bad but whatever happened to the classic action heroes? When's there going to be a big budget flick about Basilone?

I liked it quite a bit, but it had a few flaws (especially in the beginning). A lot of the dialogue was kinda cheesy and too on-the-nose, especially the opening few scenes which were giving me flashbacks of Dewie Cox. The beginning of the film was really carried by Hugo Weaving, who I thought was completely fantastic. The cliches lessened but kept popping up as the film went on, like the bog standard 'introducing the team' scene in the barracks.

All that said, the action scenes were absolutely fantastic. The only real complaint I would have with them is that they were kind of horrifying yet fun in a way that felt out of tune with the serious tone in the rest of the movie. Fantastic stunts, effects and cinematography but (kind of like Fury) it started to make me feel like I was watching a gorefest action flick and not a serious, respectful historical one. I suspect Mel was having too much fun while making it to tone them down (not that I'm complaining, they were my favorite sequences).

Overall, I'm really glad to see Mel Gibson back at work and surprised that I didn't hate Andrew Garfield- though his hair is still too tall.
